headline: IBM has answered investors' fears that Anthropic's new coding tool threatens its mainframe business.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: the IBM share drop and Anthropic's COBOL post date from 23 Feb 2026, so this is older news republished.
importance_line: IBM's customers and shareholders saw a one-day fall in February over fears of AI code tools; this republished item adds IBM's reply but nothing new for today.
summary: Stocktwits reports that IBM replied to the 13.2% share fall that followed Anthropic's announcement that its Claude Code tool can help modernize COBOL, an old programming language still used on many bank mainframes. IBM said "new AI tools emerge every week" and that translating COBOL is "the easy part" compared with redesigning data and systems; this is a reaction to a February event, not a new one.
notes: Older news re-dated: Google News lists CNBC and Bloomberg (23 Feb 2026) and Tom's Hardware (24 Feb 2026) on the same 13% IBM drop; the Stocktwits page itself carries a "Nvidia Q4 Earnings Preview" link and no October date. Reply story: IBM answers an Anthropic announcement; the earlier story is Anthropic's blog post on COBOL modernization with Claude Code (Monday 23 Feb 2026), which sent IBM shares down 13.2%, its worst day since October 2000. We did not carry it in our 3 Oct edition; named here for the reader. Jefferies argued the threat is overstated.
